author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory lists each specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only page at GET /specialties.html lists every specialty by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it named by full name (first name then last name); all on one page, no pagination, reachable by URL alone.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html lists every specialty by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it named by full name (first name then last name)
A veterinarian holding no specialty does not appear anywhere on the page
All specialties render on a single page with no pagination
Specialties are listed in a stable order and the veterinarians within each specialty in a stable order
A specialty held by no veterinarian appears with no veterinarians named
The page is reachable by its URL alone; this slice adds no navigation entry and no link from another page
non_goals: A visible entry point: navigation item or link from another page (deferred to a possible follow-up)
notes: Distinct from REQ-VET-001, which lists veterinarians with their specialties, paginated, and reachable via navigation. REQ-VET-003 inverts the grouping to specialty-first, single page, URL-only entry. Ordering and the empty-specialty display are open questions taking the narrowest reading for this slice — see docs/prd.md Open Questions.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the existing vet feature package and the server-rendered MVC shape (system-design.md Overview and Contracts). It is the specialty-first inversion of REQ-VET-001's vet-first directory. New route GET /specialties.html on VetController; new SpecialtyRepository mirroring owner/PetTypeRepository (a name-ordered @Query over a lookup value); new template templates/vets/specialtyList.html. No service layer (per current architecture), no ADR (follows the PetTypeRepository precedent exactly, no trade-off). system-design.md Contracts table updated: added SpecialtyRepository row, wired REQ-VET-003 into VetController and Specialty. Because a specialty held by no veterinarian must still appear, the specialty list must come from SpecialtyRepository, not be derived from the vets — VetRepository.findAll only surfaces held specialties. This is why I recommend a new SpecialtyRepository over the prd-entry's advisory file_target of VetRepository (VetRepository is bound to the Vet aggregate; a specialty-listing query does not belong there, and PetTypeRepository is the established home for a lookup-value listing).
integration_points: GET /specialties.html renders view vets/specialtyList (mirror /vets.html; NO second @ResponseBody route — that was the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 artifact, do not replicate)
VetController gains a SpecialtyRepository constructor dependency alongside VetRepository

Controller assembles the specialty-first view model: start from SpecialtyRepository (all specialties, name order), then attach the veterinarians whose Vet.getSpecialties() contains each specialty, drawn from VetRepository.findAll()
Template reuses layout fragment with menu selector 'vets' — no new nav entry, satisfying the URL-only-entry constraint

REQ-LANG-002 message-key parity: reuse existing keys #{specialties}, #{vets}, #{none} (all present in messages.properties). Specialty and vet names are data, rendered unescaped-safe by Thymeleaf's default escaping. Introducing any NEW #{key} obliges adding it to all eleven locale bundles or the bundle-parity build test fails.

patterns.description: lookup-value repository with a name-ordered @Query (SELECT s FROM Specialty s ORDER BY s.name) — the template for SpecialtyRepository
@GetMapping HTML-list route returning a view name with model attributes — the template for the /specialties.html method
Vet.getSpecialties() already returns specialties name-sorted; the association is EAGER and owned by Vet, so findAll() carries the holdings needed for the inversion

@WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean repository stub is the sanctioned web-slice harness (testing-principles.md: framework stub tolerated for the existing suite); add a @MockitoBean SpecialtyRepository and follow this pattern

risks.risk: Entity identity equality: BaseEntity does not override equals/hashCode by value, so a Map<Specialty,List<Vet>> keyed by Specialty is fragile for grouping and de-dup
risks.mitigation: Build the view model as an ordered List of a small presentation row (e.g. record holding the specialty name and its ordered List<Vet>), not a Map keyed by an entity; primes every specialty so empty ones render with no vets

risks.risk: Stable ordering is unspecified by the PRD (open question 1) — an arbitrary order fails the specialtiesAndVeterinariansAppearInStableOrder test
risks.mitigation: Specialties in name order (from the repository @Query); veterinarians within each specialty sorted deterministically, e.g. Comparator.comparing(Vet::getLastName).thenComparing(Vet::getFirstName). Display each vet as first-name-then-last-name per the acceptance criterion

risks.risk: Grouping/inversion could be read as a business rule placed in a controller (the flagged architecture gap, Open Questions #2)
risks.mitigation: This is presentation-model assembly, not a domain invariant — it belongs in the controller under the current architecture. Keep the template dumb (iterate the pre-assembled rows); the model attribute is what the WebMvcTest asserts on

notes: ADR not warranted: the design reuses the PetTypeRepository lookup-repository precedent and the existing HTML-list controller shape with no hard-to-reverse trade-off. Scope guard: read-only; no write path, NG-2 unchanged; do not add a navigation entry or a machine-readable second route. Recommended next agent: feature-implementer. No design-doc-autofix records in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op this dispatch.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The five new tests were written after the 2026-07-31 cutoff and must follow the BDD naming school mandated in testing-principles.md § Test Naming: `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`. The current names are descriptive imperative phrases rather than the prescribed form. Rename: specialtyDirectoryListsEachSpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians → theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEachSpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians; veterinarianHoldingNoSpecialtyDoesNotAppear → aVeterinarianHoldingNoSpecialtyShouldNotAppear; allSpecialtiesRenderOnOnePageWithoutPagination → theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePageWithoutPagination; specialtiesAndVeterinariansAppearInStableOrder → theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListSpecialtiesAndVeterinariansInStableOrder; specialtyHeldByNoVeterinarianAppearsWithNoneNamed → aSpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarianShouldAppearWithNoneNamed.
findings.fix: Rename each method using the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} pattern as shown in the description.

findings.description: specialtyDirectoryListsEachSpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians asserts that Linda Douglas appears for surgery but does not assert that Rafael Ortega also appears. The fixture gives surgery two holders (linda() and rafael()), and the PRD acceptance criterion is 'each specialty listed with the veterinarians holding it' — plural. The ordering test (line 171) implies Rafael is present by asserting his name follows Linda, but the primary spec test that establishes 'holders shown' should independently assert all holders of a multi-vet specialty. Add containsString("Rafael Ortega") to this test.

specialtyHeldByNoVeterinarianAppearsWithNoneNamed asserts containsString("none") without scoping the check to the dentistry row. The test checks that 'none' appears anywhere on the page, not that it appears in the context of the dentistry specialty. If 'none' were to appear elsewhere on the rendered layout for unrelated reasons, the test would pass even if dentistry rendered an empty cell. The assertion is technically correct for the English locale (messages.properties maps key 'none' to the literal 'none') but is weaker than the spec demands. A stronger assertion would verify 'none' appears in textual proximity to 'dentistry', for example by extracting the body and using an AssertJ index comparison: assertThat(body.indexOf("none")).isGreaterThan(body.indexOf("dentistry")).
findings.fix: Extract the response body via .andReturn().getResponse().getContentAsString() and add an AssertJ assertion that body.indexOf("none") is greater than body.indexOf("dentistry") and less than body.indexOf("radiology"), confirming 'none' is in the dentistry row and not elsewhere.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The `new ArrayList<>()` defensive copy of the `findAll()` result is never mutated — `allVets` is only read via stream filter. The copy costs an allocation and makes the reader wonder whether a mutation follows. The result of `findAll()` can be used directly in the stream pipeline.
findings.fix: Replace `new ArrayList<>(this.vetRepository.findAll())` with `this.vetRepository.findAll()` and remove the `ArrayList` import if it becomes unused; keep `Comparator` and the rest of the method unchanged.

findings.description: The vet-name span uses the self-closing form `` on a non-void HTML element. HTML5 parsers ignore the `/>` and treat the tag as open; Thymeleaf's HTML mode rendering happens to close it correctly in practice (tests pass), but the template source is non-standard and may surprise an editor or future reader. The companion `none` already uses the conventional form.
findings.fix: Change `` to ``.

The `holds()` helper correctly matches by specialty name rather than entity identity, with an explanatory comment that names the reason

All five PRD acceptance criteria are covered by named tests with clear, spec-grounded names; tests exercise negative cases (no-specialty vet absent, empty-specialty row with 'none') and ordering

Constructor injection with no @Autowired annotation, consistent with the rest of the controller

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: The Specialty directory narrative paragraph closes with implementation-phasing language that does not belong in durable PRD prose: 'this slice adds no navigation entry and no link from another page, and a visible entry point may follow as a separate request.' The phrase 'this slice' couples the PRD to the harness pipeline's slice model; 'may follow as a separate request' uses product-ticket language. Both concepts are already carried correctly: the behavioral constraint (no nav entry) belongs in the prose as a system fact, and the open question about a future entry point is recorded in the Open Questions section at line 201. The narrative sentence should state the system's current behavior without phasing language.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence 'The page is reached by its own address alone: this slice adds no navigation entry and no link from another page, and a visible entry point may follow as a separate request.' with: 'The page is reached by its own address alone; the specialty directory adds no navigation entry and no link from another page.'
